lanes.summary: The diff implements RankedTensor<D, L> as described, migrates the crate's own dynamic matmul onto the typed kernel, adds 12 trybuild compile-fail cases (exceeds the ≥8 requirement) plus a pass-suite, adds the CLAUDE.md line with correctly scoped language, and the error-message-preservation test genuinely covers the rank-mismatch and contraction-mismatch paths against the old einsum route. No unrelated or forbidden changes found; aprender-tensor remains an unconsumed workspace member (confirmed via grep), which the receipt's CLAUDE.md text is careful to scope correctly ("the type covers only this crate"), so it isn't overclaiming a broader LAYOUT-001 fix.

findings.claim: Acceptance table marks 'Zero runtime cost for the migrated path' as MET, but the receipt's own benchmark shows the migrated `matmul` (dynamic path) is ~14% slower than the typed `Matrix::matmul` kernel at n=16 and n=256 due to the `from_dynamic` copy.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller invoking the migrated `aprender_tensor::matmul(&Tensor, &Tensor)` on small/large matrices pays a measurable copy overhead vs. calling `Matrix::matmul` directly — contradicting a literal reading of 'zero runtime cost' / 'compiles to the same code as the untyped one', even though the receipt discloses the gap in prose one line down.
findings.fix: Either mark this criterion 'PARTIALLY MET' instead of 'MET', or narrow the acceptance criterion in the roadmap entry to 'the typed kernel itself pays no rank-check cost' (which is what's actually proven).
